claims.claim: A resident is present 183+ days in a year, or has a rented home on a fixed-term lease

sources.name: Law on Personal Income Tax No. 109/2025/QH15 (English translation, VN Law Firm)
sources.says: Art. 29(1): the law "enters into force on July 01, 2026". Art. 2(2): resident if present "at least 183 days in 01 calendar year" (or 12 consecutive months) or with "a regular residence in Vietnam", including a house leased under a fixed-term contract. Art. 12(1): capital investment income taxed at 5%; Art. 4(6) exempts "interest on deposit at credit institutions". Art. 13(2): 0.1% of the transfer price on securities; Art. 13(1): capital transfers 20% of the gain (2% of the price if cost unknown). Arts. 3(9) and 18: inheritances of securities, business stakes, real estate and registered assets, 10% on the value above VND 20 million each time.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

claims.claim: Vietnam has no retirement or passive-income visa

sources.name: GetWhereNext: Vietnam retirement visa 2026, the honest truth
sources.says: Dated May 19, 2026. "There is no Vietnam retirement visa." The e-visa covers up to 90 days, $25 single and $50 multiple entry; "The e-visa itself is not renewable", and extending needs an inviting or guaranteeing company, organisation or person. Tourist and e-visa holders cannot get a temporary residence card; routes are qualifying work, a TT family visa (spouse of a Vietnamese citizen; card up to 3 years) or the ĐT3 investor route, VND 3 billion to under 50 billion in an active Vietnamese company (card up to 3 years).

sources.name: Viet An Law: Vietnam's proposed 10-year golden visa
